Examples

Help › Examples opens eleven complete sheets, whose comments explain each step. An example opens as a new, unsaved sheet named "Example: …", so an edit changes no file. The sweep example opens in the Sweep view and runs.

The eleven examples

ExampleThe problem it solvesWalked through in
1. First sheet: equations and unitsThe final volume and temperature of a gas that expands at constant pressure, with no fluid properties.Writing a sheet
2. States and properties (water)Four states of water at 15 bar, from compressed liquid to superheated vapor, and property functions.States and diagrams
3. Rankine cycleThe net work, thermal efficiency and back work ratio of a Rankine cycle whose turbine has an isentropic efficiency.A complete cycle
4. Vapor-compression refrigeration (R-134a)The refrigerating capacity, compressor power and COP of a refrigeration cycle whose compressor has an isentropic efficiency.Below
5. Gas turbine (air)The thermal efficiency and back work ratio of a Brayton cycle in air, with variable specific heats and two component efficiencies.Below
6. SweepsThe Rankine cycle of example 3 run for turbine inlet temperatures from 400 °C to 600 °C.Sweeps
7. Moist air: cooling with dehumidificationThe condensate and the cooling load of a dehumidifier that cools moist air below its dew point.Moist air
8. Heat exchanger with two fluidsThe states of R-134a and of water in an evaporator where the R-134a cools a stream of water.Two fluids
9. Filling a tank from a steam lineThe mass that enters a rigid, insulated tank, and its final temperature, when steam from a line fills it.Below
10. Maximum performance of a refrigeratorThe greatest COP between two reservoirs, the least power for a cooling load, and whether a claimed COP is possible.Below
11. Mixing chamber: entropy productionThe exit state of a tank where steam and cold water mix, and the rate of entropy production.Below

Vapor-compression refrigeration

Saturated R-134a vapor at -16 °C enters a compressor with an isentropic efficiency of 0.8 and leaves at 9 bar. Saturated liquid leaves the condenser and is throttled to the evaporator. The mass flow rate is 0.06 kg/s.

%% Vapor-compression refrigeration with R-134a
% Saturated vapor enters the compressor; saturated liquid leaves the
% condenser and is throttled to the evaporator pressure.
fluid r134a

%% Given values
T_e   = -16 [C]        % evaporator temperature
p_k   = 9 [bar]        % condenser pressure
eta_c = 0.8            % compressor isentropic efficiency
m_dot = 0.06 [kg/s]    % refrigerant mass flow rate

%% States
% No pressure drop in the evaporator and condenser: states 4 and 1 are
% at T_e, states 2 and 3 at p_k.
state 1  : T = T_e, x = 1
% State 2s: the compressor exit if the compression were isentropic.
state 2s : p = p_k, s = s_1
% The actual compressor exit enthalpy follows from the efficiency.
eta_c = (h_2s - h_1) / (h_2 - h_1)
state 2  : p = p_k, h = h_2
state 3  : p = p_k, x = 0
% Throttling valve: steady state, no stray heat transfer, no work, kinetic
% and potential energy changes neglected, so h is unchanged.
state 4  : T = T_e, h = h_3

%% Rates
% Each component: steady state, kinetic and potential energy changes
% neglected. Each amount is positive, with its direction in its name.
% Evaporator, no work. Q_in: refrigerating capacity, Q̇_in.
Q_in  = m_dot * (h_1 - h_4)    % refrigerating capacity
% Compressor, no stray heat transfer. W_c: compressor power, Ẇ_c.
W_c   = m_dot * (h_2 - h_1)    % compressor power
% Condenser, no work. Q_out: heat transfer rate from the refrigerant, Q̇_out.
Q_out = m_dot * (h_2 - h_3)    % condenser heat transfer rate
COP   = Q_in / W_c             % coefficient of performance

%% Energy balance of the cycle
check Q_out == Q_in + W_c

%% p-h diagram
% -h- draws the throttling process at constant enthalpy.
plot ph : 1 -s- 2 -p- 3 -h- 4 -p- 1
% Set eta_c = 1 for the ideal cycle and compare COP.

Dome gives h_2 = 284.18 kJ/kg, T_2 = 51.43 °C and x_4 = 0.338. Then Q_in = 8.3542 kW, W_c = 2.7235 kW, Q_out = 11.078 kW and COP = 3.0675.

  1. fluid r134a sets the fluid. A temperature and a quality fix state 1: T = T_e, x = 1 is saturated vapor at -16 °C.
  2. For a compressor, the isentropic enthalpy rise is the numerator of the efficiency: (h_2s - h_1) / (h_2 - h_1).
  3. The throttling valve leaves h unchanged, so h = h_3 fixes state 4 with T_e.
  4. Each balance is multiplied by m_dot, so the amounts are rates, in kW.
  5. plot ph : 1 -s- 2 -p- 3 -h- 4 -p- 1 draws a p–h diagram. -h- draws the throttling at constant h.
  6. The last line suggests eta_c = 1, the ideal cycle. W_c falls to 2.1788 kW and COP rises to 3.8343.

Gas turbine

Air enters the compressor at 290 K and 95 kPa, with a pressure ratio of 12, and the turbine at 1300 K. The compressor efficiency is 0.84 and the turbine efficiency 0.88.

%% Gas turbine (air-standard Brayton cycle)
% Air is an ideal gas with variable specific heats. The compressor and
% the turbine each have an isentropic efficiency.
fluid air

%% Given values
T_1   = 290 [K]
p_1   = 95 [kPa]
r_p   = 12             % compressor pressure ratio
T_3   = 1300 [K]       % turbine inlet temperature
eta_c = 0.84
eta_t = 0.88

%% States
% No pressure drop in the combustor and the exhaust heat exchanger: states 2
% and 3 are at p_2, states 4 and 1 at p_1.
state 1  : p = p_1, T = T_1
% State 2s: the compressor exit if the compression were isentropic.
state 2s : p = r_p * p_1, s = s_1
% The actual compressor exit enthalpy follows from the efficiency.
eta_c = (h_2s - h_1) / (h_2 - h_1)
state 2  : p = p_2s, h = h_2
state 3  : p = p_2, T = T_3
% State 4s: the turbine exit if the expansion were isentropic.
state 4s : p = p_1, s = s_3
% The actual turbine exit enthalpy follows from the efficiency.
eta_t = (h_3 - h_4) / (h_3 - h_4s)
state 4  : p = p_1, h = h_4

%% Work and heat transfer per unit mass of air
% Each component: steady state, kinetic and potential energy changes
% neglected. Each amount is positive, with its direction in its name.
% Compressor, no stray heat transfer. w_c: compressor work per unit mass
% flowing, Ẇ_c/ṁ.
w_c   = h_2 - h_1      % compressor
% Turbine, no stray heat transfer. w_t: turbine work per unit mass, Ẇ_t/ṁ.
w_t   = h_3 - h_4      % turbine
% Combustor, no work. q_in: heat transfer to the air per unit mass, Q̇_in/ṁ.
q_in  = h_3 - h_2      % combustor
% Heat exchanger, no work. q_out: heat transfer from the air per unit
% mass, Q̇_out/ṁ.
q_out = h_4 - h_1      % exhaust heat exchanger
% w_net: net work per unit mass, Ẇ_cycle/ṁ.
w_net = w_t - w_c

%% Performance
eta = w_net / q_in     % thermal efficiency
bwr = w_c / w_t        % back work ratio

%% Energy balance of the cycle
check q_in - q_out == w_net

%% T-s diagram
plot Ts : 1 -s- 2 -p- 3 -s- 4 -p- 1
% Lower eta_c to 0.75 and watch bwr and eta.

Dome gives h_2 = 647.67 kJ/kg (T_2 = 638.47 K) and h_4 = 787.47 kJ/kg (T_4 = 768.45 K). Then w_net = 250.9 kJ/kg, eta = 0.33532 and bwr = 0.58764.

  1. fluid air treats air as an ideal gas with variable specific heats. Its state lines are written as for water.
  2. A property may be an expression: p = r_p * p_1 gives state 2s the compressor exit pressure.
  3. State 2 takes the pressure of state 2s, p = p_2s. State 3 takes that of state 2, since the combustor has no pressure drop.
  4. Each efficiency line has one unknown, h_2 or h_4. The work and heat transfer lines after them are written as in the Rankine cycle, one line per component.
  5. The last line suggests eta_c = 0.75. Then bwr rises to 0.65815 and eta falls to 0.29489.

Filling a tank from a steam line

A rigid, insulated tank of 0.4 m³ holds steam at 1.5 bar and 160 °C. Steam at 10 bar and 320 °C flows in from a line until the tank reaches 10 bar.

%% Filling a tank from a steam line
% A rigid, insulated tank of 0.4 m³ holds steam at 1.5 bar and 160 °C. A
% valve to a line carrying steam at 10 bar and 320 °C is opened, and steam
% flows in until the pressure in the tank reaches the line pressure. The
% state of the steam in the line does not change.
fluid water

%% Given values
V   = 0.4 [m^3]     % tank volume
p_1 = 1.5 [bar]     % in the tank at the start
T_1 = 160 [C]
p_i = 10 [bar]      % in the line
T_i = 320 [C]
p_2 = p_i           % in the tank at the end

%% States
state 1 : p = p_1, T = T_1     % in the tank at the start
state i : p = p_i, T = T_i     % in the line, where the steam enters
% State 2 is fixed by p_2 and the u_2 the energy balance gives.
state 2 : p = p_2, u = u_2     % in the tank at the end

%% Mass in the tank
m_1 = V / v_1
m_2 = V / v_2

%% Mass and energy balances over the filling
% Control volume: the tank, with one inlet and no exit. The mass that
% enters, m_i, is the increase in the mass in the tank.
m_i = m_2 - m_1
% No heat transfer (insulated tank), no work (rigid, no shaft), kinetic
% and potential energy neglected. Each kilogram that enters carries the
% enthalpy h_i, which is the same throughout because the line state does
% not change.
m_2*u_2 - m_1*u_1 = m_i*h_i

%% Check
% The steam that enters brings h_i = u_i + p_i v_i: its internal energy
% and the flow work done to push it in. The steam in the tank ends hotter
% than the steam in the line.
check T_2 > T_i

%% T-s diagram
% The 10 bar isobar from the line state i to the final state 2. It is not
% a process the steam follows; it shows where state 2 lies.
plot Ts : i -p- 2
% Change p_1 to 1 bar, or T_1 to 120 °C, and watch m_i and T_2.

Dome gives m_1 = 0.30359 kg, m_2 = 1.2823 kg and m_i = 0.97876 kg. The states table gives T_2 = 411.12 °C, and the check T_2 > T_i passes.

  1. The control volume is the tank, with one inlet and no exit. The balances are written over the whole filling, from state 1 to state 2.
  2. A label may be a letter: state i is the steam in the line, where it enters.
  3. u = u_2 fixes state 2 with p_2, and the energy balance finds u_2. Dome solves the balance and state 2 together.
  4. plot Ts : i -p- 2 draws the 10 bar isobar from i to 2. It is not a process the steam follows; it shows where state 2 lies.
  5. The last line suggests p_1 = 1 [bar]. Then m_i = 1.038 kg and T_2 = 433.67 °C.

Maximum performance of a refrigerator

A freezer keeps its compartment at -18 °C in a kitchen at 22 °C, and energy leaks in at 150 W. A maker claims a COP of 5.5.

%% Maximum performance of a refrigerator
% A freezer keeps its compartment at -18 °C in a kitchen at 22 °C. Energy
% leaks into the compartment at 150 W, and the refrigeration cycle
% removes it at the same rate. The second law bounds every refrigeration
% cycle between these two temperatures, whatever its working fluid.

%% Given values
T_C     = -18 [C]      % cold reservoir: the freezer compartment
T_H     = 22 [C]       % hot reservoir: the kitchen
Q_dot_C = 150 [W]      % heat transfer rate from the compartment

%% Maximum coefficient of performance
% No refrigeration cycle between two reservoirs has a greater COP than a
% reversible one, and every reversible one has the same COP, which
% depends on the reservoir temperatures alone. Dome holds temperatures
% in kelvin, so T_C / (T_H - T_C) is a ratio of absolute temperatures.
COP_max = T_C / (T_H - T_C)

%% Least power input
% COP = Q_dot_C / W_dot, so for a given cooling load the least power
% input W_dot_min is that of a reversible cycle.
W_dot_min = Q_dot_C / COP_max
% Energy balance of the cycle at steady state: the heat transfer rate to
% the kitchen, Q_dot_H, is the rate removed plus the power input.
Q_dot_H = Q_dot_C + W_dot_min

%% A claimed refrigerator
% A maker claims a COP of 5.5 for a freezer between the same
% temperatures, which would need this power input.
COP_claim   = 5.5
W_dot_claim = Q_dot_C / COP_claim

%% Check
% A claim above COP_max is impossible: it would need less power than a
% reversible cycle.
check COP_claim <= COP_max
% Change T_C to -30 °C, as in a deep freezer: COP_max falls below the
% claim and the check fails.

Dome gives COP_max = 6.3787, W_dot_min = 0.023516 kW and W_dot_claim = 0.027273 kW. The check passes: 5.5 <= 6.3787.

  1. The sheet has no fluid and no states. It uses only the two temperatures and the rates.
  2. T_C and T_H are given in °C, and Dome holds them in kelvin. So T_C / (T_H - T_C) is a ratio of absolute temperatures, 255.15 K over 40 K.
  3. Dome shows a power in kW: W_dot_min = 0.023516 kW is 23.5 W.
  4. The last line suggests T_C = -30 [C]. COP_max falls to 4.676, and the check fails: 5.5 not <= 4.676.

Mixing chamber: entropy production

Saturated water vapor at 0.1 kg/s and liquid water at 15 °C and 1.5 kg/s enter an insulated tank. Warm water leaves it, and every stream is at 1 bar.

%% Mixing chamber: entropy production
% A hot-water tank is fed by a steam line: saturated water vapor and cold
% liquid water enter the insulated tank, and warm water leaves it. Every
% stream is at 1 bar. The rate of entropy production measures how
% irreversible the mixing is.
fluid water

%% Given values
p       = 1 [bar]       % every stream, no pressure drop
m_dot_1 = 0.1 [kg/s]    % steam
m_dot_2 = 1.5 [kg/s]    % cold water

%% States
state 1 : p = p, x = 1          % saturated vapor in
state 2 : p = p, T = 15 [C]     % cold water in
% State 3 is fixed by p and the h_3 the energy balance gives.
state 3 : p = p, h = h_3        % warm water out

%% Mass and energy balances
% Control volume: the tank, at steady state, with two inlets and one
% exit. No heat transfer (insulated), no work, kinetic and potential
% energy changes neglected.
m_dot_3 = m_dot_1 + m_dot_2
m_dot_3*h_3 = m_dot_1*h_1 + m_dot_2*h_2

%% Entropy balance
% The same control volume. With no heat transfer, entropy enters and
% leaves only with the streams; what leaves beyond what enters is
% produced inside. sigma_dot: rate of entropy production.
0 = m_dot_1*s_1 + m_dot_2*s_2 - m_dot_3*s_3 + sigma_dot

%% Check
% Entropy production is positive in every actual process and zero only
% in a reversible one.
check sigma_dot > 0 [kW/K]

%% T-s diagram
% The three states lie on the 1 bar isobar, the exit between the two
% inlets. The line is not a process.
plot Ts : 2 -p- 3 -p- 1
% Raise m_dot_1 to 0.2 kg/s and watch T_3 and sigma_dot.

Dome gives h_3 = 226.39 kJ/kg and sigma_dot = 0.13663 kW/K. The states table gives T_3 = 54.041 °C.

  1. The tank has two inlets and one exit. h = h_3 fixes state 3 with p, and the energy balance finds h_3.
  2. The entropy balance has no heat transfer term, since the tank is insulated. What leaves beyond what enters is sigma_dot, produced inside.
  3. The check sigma_dot > 0 [kW/K] holds for every actual process.
  4. The last line suggests m_dot_1 = 0.2 [kg/s]. Then T_3 = 88.405 °C and sigma_dot = 0.18792 kW/K.
